# `js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types`

**JSDoc types name something defined**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/jsdoc` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `defined_types`, `globals`, `env` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the definition or import is the author's) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/no-undefined-types` |

## What it checks

A name used in a tag's `{type}` — or in an `@augments` / `@extends` — is defined: declared in the file (a variable, function, class, interface, type alias, enum, namespace, import or type parameter, in any scope), named by a `@typedef`, `@callback`, `@class` or other tag that defines a namepath, by a `@template` or an `@import` of the file, by a `/* globals … */` comment, by the rule's `defined_types` or `globals` options, by a data table of an environment named in `env`, or built in: JavaScript's globals, TypeScript's lib types (`Partial`, `Record`, `Awaited`, …) and the type keywords. The root of a dotted name (`Foo.Bar`) has to be defined. A type parameter of a function type, and an `infer` name, count within the type. As in the plugin, the environment's globals (the DOM, Node) are not defined unless `env` says so. Not read: the namepaths of other tags (`@memberof`, `@fires`, …), `checkUsedTypedefs` and `markVariablesAsUsed`.

**Why:** A type that names nothing is read as `any` by TypeScript and as an error by every documentation tool, and it is usually a typo or a missing import.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/jsdoc` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/jsdoc"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defined_types` | `string[]` | `[]` | type names to treat as defined |
| `globals` | `string[]` | `[]` | global names to treat as defined |
| `env` | `string[]` | `[]` | environments whose globals are defined: browser, node, commonjs, worker, serviceworker, shared-node-browser, jest, mocha, vitest |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
defined_types = []
globals = []
env = []
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = { severity = "error", options = { defined_types = ["Foo"], globals = ["<name>"], env = ["browser"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `defined_types`

*string[]* · default `[]`

type names to treat as defined

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
defined_types = ["Foo"]
```

#### `globals`

*string[]* · default `[]`

global names to treat as defined

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
globals = ["<name>"]
```

#### `env`

*string[]* · default `[]`

environments whose globals are defined: browser, node, commonjs, worker, serviceworker, shared-node-browser, jest, mocha, vitest

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
env = ["browser"]
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### defined_types

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
defined_types = ["Foo"]
```

```js
/**
 * @param {Foo} a
 */
function f(a) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a DOM type with the browser environment

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types".options]
env = ["browser"]
```

```js
/**
 * @param {HTMLElement} a
 */
function f(a) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = { options = { defined_types = ["Foo"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types" = { severity = "warn", options = { defined_types = ["Foo"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"defined_types": ["Foo"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-no-undefined-types  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>               # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Import or declare the type, or add a `@typedef` for it.
2. Name an environment in the rule's `env` option when the type is one of its globals.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
/**
 * @param {Usr} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

#### Do

```js
/**
 * @param {User} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
/**
 * @param {Usr} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

#### Do

```jsx
/**
 * @param {User} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
/**
 * @param {Usr} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

#### Do

```ts
/**
 * @param {User} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
/**
 * @param {Usr} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```

#### Do

```tsx
/**
 * @param {User} user
 */
function greet(user) {}
class User {}
```
